deliverable: Part-3 V2 production policy audit: Quality Gate B_wape <= 0.60 provenance and production decision

audited_criterion.description: B cohort WAPE (sustained high-volume, the business-critical segment)
audited_criterion.justification_verbatim: B cohort is the monetarily dominant segment. Reference 0.51-0.55; 0.60 bound rejects >~10% regression on high-volume products.

key_findings: Canonical source is src/models/quality_gate.py (Phase-D threshold table), mirrored verbatim in lifecycle and posthoc reports.

Reference values are validation metrics of pre-V2 candidates: persisted winner (EXP0) val B WAPE 0.5485 and EXP2 (= V2) val B WAPE 0.5102, per reports/experiments/06_forecasting_controlled_experiments_report.md.
0.60 is a regression guard above the measured reference band 0.51-0.55 (0.60/0.55 = +9.4%, 0.60/0.5102 = +17.6%); stated '>~10% regression' reads off the reference high-end.
The module itself labels ONLY the cohort-bias bounds (B_bias_pct >= -20, B2_bias_pct >= -20) as 'business requirement'; all WAPE bounds are framed as reference-anchored tolerance bands.

The 'monetarily dominant segment' premise appears ONLY in the gate justification text and verbatim copies; no revenue/price-weighted analysis exists in the repository (in units, B is ~6% of validation sum-actual; C is ~89%).
Threshold was pre-registered relative to the Test split (Phase-D table from validation references, shipped before any Test evaluation; lifecycle and posthoc reports state thresholds UNCHANGED).
No explicit stakeholder/business requirement artifact exists in the repository (no business requirements doc; only MLflow pip requirements.txt files).
phase1_provenance.pre_registration_status: pre-registered relative to Test; not reverse-engineered to the post-hoc result

phase2_b_cohort.definition: B-sustained = train pos weeks >= 6 and avg weekly demand >= 1.0; B2-mid = pos >= 6 and avg >= 0.5 (not B); C-long-tail = rest

business_significance.role: sustained high-demand 'best seller' stratum; the visibility cohort where the delivery requirement of the experiment cycle is judged
business_significance.why_separate_threshold: cohort-specific gating preserves segment identity and prevents sacrificing the long tail for segment gains (C_wape justification)
business_significance.consequence_of_high_wape: within the 2:1 cost-of-error framework, under-forecast-dominated high WAPE on B = lost sales/stockouts on best sellers (val: 30% B rows carry 68% of B error)
business_significance.test_window_nuance: on the post-hoc Test run B bias is +9.85% (over-forecast) and B2 +0.86%; the documented stockout mechanism does NOT manifest on Test
business_significance.business_critical_vs_diagnostic: narrative labels B as business-critical ('economically important products', 'monetarily dominant'); repository evidence substantiates B as the analytic sustained-demand stratum and a small (37-product) high-visibility unit bundle, but independent economic significance (revenue weighting) is asserted, not computed

finding_small_cohort_sampling.summary: B is only 37 independent product series; per-split WAPE is sample-sensitive; val 0.510 sits just below 0.60 while Test 0.628 crosses it despite better global Test WAPE and B2 (harder on val, 0.5557) NOT failing on Test.
finding_small_cohort_sampling.source: part3_b_cohort_error_analysis.md hypothesis H4 ('Contributory to explain the gate outcome, not the error mechanism')
finding_small_cohort_sampling.caveat: only one Test realization exists, so the crossing cannot be proven to be sampling noise alone; equally consistent with genuine regression on that window.

conclusion: 0.60 has no independently justified business interpretation in-repo (engineering regression guard, unevidenced 'monetarily dominant' label).
The criterion that fails on Test is an engineering tolerance, while the documented business requirement (bias >= -20%) passes.
No better model exists today: all three validation-only interventions returned NO_VALID_IMPROVEMENT.
Any new numeric bound chosen from V2's result would violate the no-threshold-tuning rule; thus no number may be proposed as an engineer-side fix.
Keeping 0.60 is defensible as the conservative status quo; the evidence does not justify an automatic change.

phase4_production_decision.not_A_rationale: B_wape<=0.60 is demonstrably not a genuine documented business requirement (module attaches that label to bias bounds, not WAPE bounds); 'monetarily dominant' premise unevidenced; single-split gating of a 37-product cohort is statistically fragile as a hard rule.
phase4_production_decision.not_C_rationale: repository contains no documented ALTERNATIVE gate formulation already grounded in business requirements; the documented business requirements (bias>= -20%, asym21) are separate existing criteria, not an alternative formulation; crafting one now IS the policy decision that belongs under B.
phase4_production_decision.operational_effect: V2 remains Staging; gate unchanged; no promotion; no V3
required_policy_decision: Confirm or reject the premise 'B = monetarily dominant segment' (with revenue evidence or explicit owner sign-off).

Decide how a 37-product single-split per-cohort WAPE may be gated: (i) keep current regression-guard form, (ii) treat bias/stockout rule as the sole B business requirement with WAPE regression routed to a diagnostic non-blocking track, or (iii) adopt a variance-aware/robust multi-split formulation.

Any chosen formulation must be pre-registered and applied prospectively to all future candidates; a fresh evaluation of V2 under a new policy is allowed only as a clearly-labeled policy re-read, never as a rewrite of the historical FAIL.
If (i) is reaffirmed, 0.60 stays enforced, V2 stays Staging, and a future Robust Loss intervention becomes eligible only as a separate validation-only pre-registered experiment (none started now).

distinctions.historical_gate_definition: Phase-D table: 12 numeric + 7 technical criteria; B_wape <= 0.60 as reference-anchored regression guard (pre-registered before Test).
distinctions.validation_gate_result: PASS on all 19 criteria (B_wape 0.5101 <= 0.60); v2 provisionally to Production.
distinctions.posthoc_holdout_result: FAIL on B_wape 0.6282 > 0.60 (sole failing criterion of 19); v2 Production to Staging; classified post_hoc_holdout_evaluation, exactly once.
distinctions.business_requirement: B/B2 must not systematically under-forecast (bias >= -20%, stockout guard) plus 2:1 asymmetric cost framework; PASS on the post-hoc holdout (B +9.85%, B2 +0.86%, asym21 0.025095).
distinctions.technical_heuristic: All WAPE tolerance bands including B_wape <= 0.60 are reference-anchored engineering regression guards, not owner-specified requirements.
distinctions.production_policy: Production only when all 19 criteria pass on the held-out evaluation; V2 does not currently satisfy the policy.
distinctions.final_production_decision: B_FORMAL_GATE_REVISION_REQUIRED; blocker treated as gate-policy/provenance issue, not demonstrated model-performance failure. V2 stays Staging until an explicit owner decision.

deliverables.tests: none added (no gate-policy change; decision B leaves the gate unchanged)
